title: Root binding.gyp command substitution runs an obfuscated root index.js payload
provenance: Miasma / Phantom Gyp npm worm (June 2026): compromised packages shipped a root binding.gyp with a GYP command substitution that ran `node index.js` during node-gyp configure while package.json had no install lifecycle scripts. Public analyses reported an obfuscated multi-stage loader that later downloaded Bun, harvested CI/developer credentials, exfiltrated through GitHub repositories, and republished packages. Defanged: package names are synthetic, the JavaScript payload is an inert eval wrapper, no C2 or credential strings are present, and no executable malware is included.
intent: Models the install-time bypass: root binding.gyp is enough for npm to invoke node-gyp, and the `<!(node index.js ... && echo stub.c)` expansion executes package-owned JavaScript during configure. Drydock should catch the gyp command substitution itself, independent of whether the inner obfuscated loader can be decoded from the bounded text sample.
